title: Replacing a Clogged T-Fitting in a Double-Bowl Kitchen Sink Drain

locations.name: Under the kitchen sink (garbage disposal area)
locations.basis: Transcript describes components (disposer, tailpiece, T-fitting, trap) located under the sink; not explicit shooting location

summary: This Old House analyzes a two-bowl kitchen sink clog by tracing the drain path from the garbage disposal through the tailpiece and a T-fitting to the trap. The host identifies a plastic diverter inside the T-fitting as the blockage, disassembles the connections, and replaces the assembly with a full-size brass T-fitting (no diverter) along with new gaskets. After reassembly, the system is leak-tested and drained to confirm a clear, fast-flowing drain, with a note that deeper clogs could involve pipes leading to the basement if symptoms persist.
topics: drain path from disposer to trap

sections.title: Diagnosis and choke-point inspection under the sink
sections.description: The presenter identifies a double-bowl sink with a garbage disposal and explains that clogs may involve the disposer or the drain path. The team looks for choke points under the sink, focusing on the disposer discharge, the tailpiece, the T-fitting where the strainer meets the disposer, and the trap as key potential sites for blockage.

sections.title: Diverter and T-fitting blockage revealed
sections.description: The demonstrator isolates the T-fitting and shows a gunked-up top, explaining that a plastic diverter narrows the opening and creates a prime location for a blockage. This identifies the T-fitting/diverter as the blockage source in this setup.

sections.title: Brass tee installation and gasket details
sections.description: A full-size brass T-fitting without a diverter is installed as the replacement. The host demonstrates the new components: a gasketed tailpiece with a top gasket, a flange tailpiece, and the associated nuts, which are tightened to secure the connection. This section covers the material choices and the assembly sequence to resolve the choke point.

sections.title: Leak test and drainage verification
sections.description: After assembling, the connections are tested by filling and draining the left-hand bowl with the stopper in place. The demonstration confirms no leaks and a fast drainage rate, validating the repair.

featured_techniques.technique: Diagnosing drain clogs by tracing the path from disposer to trap and inspecting for choke points
Identifying a diverter-induced restriction inside a T-fitting as the blockage
Replacing a clogged T-fitting with a full-size brass tee (no diverter) and using appropriate gaskets
Assembling gasketed connections (top gasket, flange tailpiece) and tightening with pliers
Leak testing and functional verification using water fill, stopper, and drainage observation
